page: Microsoft Azure M416s_10_v2 is a memory-optimized enterprise instance powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system provides 416 dedicated vCPUs across 208 physical cores (2 threads per core) operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI vector instruction sets. The server includes 9496.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 22.83 GB of RAM per vCPU, accompanied by 4398 GB of local SSD temporary storage and no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory subsystem capacity alongside distinct single-thread limitations. The platform scores in the top 10% across parallel tests, achieving 350,163.22 in stress-ng multi-core CPU and 102,739.57 in PassMark CPU score. Its massive memory architecture sustains a small-block cached read bandwidth of 19,461.33 GB/sec and an uncached 256MB block read throughput of 695.9 GB/sec. Application testing shows top-tier throughput with 247.68 million Redis SET operations per second and 133.95 GB/sec static web throughput. In contrast, single-thread performance is modest, with a bottom-quartile stress-ng single-core score of 1350.27 and single-threaded gzip compression at 22.46 GB/sec.

Given its massive scale, the instance represents a specialized allocation of massive compute and memory density within a single node. While single-threaded latency and token generation speeds are lower than newer architectures, the qualitative return on scale is centered on parallel processing and in-memory capacity. The instance is suited for ultra-large in-memory database engines such as SAP HANA, massive distributed caching fabrics, multi-threaded high-performance computing simulations, and intensive ETL pipelines that require thousands of gigabytes of RAM mapped directly into a single system image.

Built on x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 support, the configuration incorporates 9496.0 GB of RAM (22.83 GB per vCPU) and 4398 GB of local SSD storage without attached GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth, reaching 350,163.22 in multi-core stress-ng tests, 695.9 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth, and 247.68 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-thread CPU performance ranks in the lower percentiles. The platform provides extreme density and throughput suited for large-scale in-memory databases like SAP HANA, massive caching layers, memory-bound simulations, and complex batch data transformation workloads.
